mainTopic: אותו ואת בנו (slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day): whether slaughter that does not produce meat a person may eat still counts as slaughter, and whether the altar 'eating' a קרבן counts as eating.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a statement that follows רבי שמעון's view: only slaughter that makes meat fit to eat counts for אותו ואת בנו. So slaughtering one animal as an עולה, which people never eat, and then the other as חולין is exempt. רבי יעקב quotes רבי יוחנן, who disagrees: the altar's 'eating' counts as eating, learned from the doubled words הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל. A new משנה then lists slaughters that never produce permitted meat, such as a טרפה, slaughter for עבודה זרה, a פרת חטאת, a שור הנסקל and an עגלה ערופה. רבי שמעון exempts in these cases and the חכמים hold him liable. In every view, an invalid שחיטה, stabbing or tearing out the organs is exempt. In the גמרא, ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about a second slaughter done for עבודה זרה when the person was warned only about אותו ואת בנו: does the greater sin cancel the lashes even without a warning? The גמרא shows they hold the same positions in רב דימי's case about death or lashes together with a money payment, and explains why both disputes had to be taught. Finally, the גמרא asks whether the slaughter of the פרת חטאת is really 'unfit', since רבי שמעון elsewhere says it can receive טומאת אוכלין. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Even slaughtering an עולה first does not make one liable
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי שמעון, if someone slaughters one animal of the pair as an עולה and then slaughters the other as חולין, he is exempt, because the first slaughter does not produce meat that people may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not only that case. Even if he slaughtered an עולה and afterward slaughtered a non-sacred animal, he is exempt. The first slaughter is not a slaughter that leads to eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a 'not only this, but even this' statement. It says that under רבי שמעון's approach, slaughtering an עולה followed by a חולין animal does not break the law of אותו ואת בנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that only slaughter which makes meat fit for eating counts as 'slaughter'. An עולה is burned completely on the altar and no person eats it, so its slaughter does not count. Without two real slaughters, there is no violation.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day
A burnt offering that is burned entirely on the altar
Ordinary, non-sacred animals
A slaughter that makes the meat fit to eat
Exempt from punishment

steps.confusionAlert: The עולה is still a fully valid קרבן. The point is only that, for רבי שמעון, its slaughter is not the kind of slaughter that counts for אותו ואת בנו.

phrases.english: But even if he slaughtered a burnt offering
and afterward slaughtered a non-sacred animal, he is exempt,
since the first slaughter
is not a slaughter that leads to eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ שָׁחַט עוֹלָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט חוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי שמעון's view, which comes before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, slaughtering an עולה and then חולין is exempt, because slaughtering an עולה is not slaughter for eating.

steps.title: The altar's 'eating' counts as eating
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב quotes רבי יוחנן: when the altar consumes a קרבן, that is considered eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the altar's eating is called eating.
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion is brought that pushes back against step 1. It says the altar consuming an offering counts as 'eating'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the altar's consumption counts as eating, then slaughtering an עולה is a שחיטה בת אכילה after all. That would make one liable for אותו ואת בנו even according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Consumption by the altar, meaning the burning of a קרבן on it
It is called (considered) eating

steps.whyThisMatters: This one idea decides whether the exemption in step 1 holds up.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Consumption by the altar is considered eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a view that disagrees with the reasoning of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The altar consuming a קרבן counts as eating.

steps.title: The proof from the doubled words הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי יוחנן's source. It answers with a פסוק about שלמים whose doubled verb points to two kinds of eating: by a person and by the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the verse says: 'And if any of the flesh of his peace offering is eaten (הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל).' The verse is talking about two kinds of eating: one is eating by a person, and one is eating by the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן holds this, and brings a פסוק as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה repeats the word for eating: הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל. The doubling is read as covering two kinds of eating. One is people eating the meat, and the other is the altar 'eating' its parts. So the altar's consumption is called eating in the תורה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק (verse)
'Be eaten, be eaten': a doubled verb that the גמרא reads as two kinds of eating
A peace offering, eaten partly by the altar and partly by people
Eating by a person

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the תורה calls the altar's consumption 'eating', learned from the doubled הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל.

phrases.english: What is the reason? Because the verse says:
"And if it is at all eaten
from the flesh of his peace offering."
The verse speaks of two kinds of eating,
phrases.notes: The word for eating is doubled in the פסוק, and that doubling is what hints at two kinds.

phrases.english: one is eating by a person
and one is eating by the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן's statement in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the altar's consumption counts as eating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:18, where the doubled verb הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל is read as two kinds of eating.

steps.title: New משנה: slaughter that never yields permitted meat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists cases where the animal slaughtered can never be eaten or used: a טרפה, slaughter for עבודה זרה, a פרת חטאת, a שור הנסקל and an עגלה ערופה. רבי שמעון exempts the slaughterer from אותו ואת בנו, and the חכמים hold him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who slaughters and the animal turns out to be a טרפה, one who slaughters for idol worship, one who slaughters the red heifer, an ox sentenced to stoning, or the heifer whose neck is broken: רבי שמעון exempts him, and the חכמים hold him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out a group of cases where the slaughter cannot lead to permitted eating, and gives the dispute about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case listed, the meat is forbidden to eat or even to benefit from. רבי שמעון stays consistent: slaughter that does not make meat fit to eat is not 'slaughter', so he exempts. The חכמים hold that any slaughter counts, so he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
Idol worship
The red heifer used for purification
An ox sentenced to stoning for killing a person
The calf whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: slaughter that cannot produce permitted meat is not slaughter for אותו ואת בנו, so he is פטור. The חכמים: it still counts, so he is חייב.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slaughters, and it is found to be a tereifa,
one who slaughters for idol worship,
and one who slaughters the red heifer,
or an ox sentenced to stoning, or a heifer whose neck is to be broken:
Rabbi Shimon exempts,
and the Rabbis hold him liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that applies the same idea of 'slaughter fit for eating' to more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In these cases רבי שמעון exempts the slaughterer from אותו ואת בנו, and the חכמים hold him liable.

steps.title: Invalid slaughter, stabbing, or tearing out: exempt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by ruling that if the שחיטה made the animal a נבלה, or if it was stabbed or its organs were torn out, there is no liability for אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters and the animal becomes a נבלה in his hand, one who stabs it, and one who tears out its organs is exempt from אותו ואת בנו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It lists acts that are not a real, valid שחיטה, so they do not break the rule of אותו ואת בנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids slaughtering a mother and its child on the same day. That word means a valid שחיטה. In these cases no proper שחיטה took place at all, so there is no 'slaughter' to count.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal became a נבלה in his hand, because the שחיטה was done wrong
One who stabs the animal's throat instead of cutting it properly
One who tears out the windpipe and food pipe instead of cutting them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the dispute in the previous step. There, the שחיטה itself was valid, but the meat could not be eaten. Here, the act was never a proper שחיטה at all.

phrases.english: One who slaughters and it becomes a carcass in his hand,
and one who stabs, and one who tears out the organs –
is exempt on account of 'it and its offspring.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's list. After the disputed cases in step 4, it gives cases where all agree he is exempt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a valid שחיטה there is no liability for אותו ואת בנו.

steps.title: Liable only when the idol slaughter came first
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש narrows the חכמים's ruling about slaughtering for עבודה זרה. They make him liable only when the first animal was for עבודה זרה and the second for his own table.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: the חכמים taught liability only when the first animal was slaughtered for עבודה זרה and the second for his table. If the first was for his table and the second for עבודה זרה, he is exempt, because he receives only the greater punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a limit that רבי שמעון בן לקיש places on the חכמים's ruling from the משנה. That ruling held a person liable when one of the animals was slaughtered for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second slaughter is for his table, that act is only אותו ואת בנו, so he gets lashes. If the second slaughter is for עבודה זרה, that one act carries both death (for עבודה זרה) and lashes. A person receives only the greater punishment, so the lashes drop away.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when..., a phrase that narrows a ruling
For his own table, meaning for ordinary eating
He receives only the greater punishment of the two

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
They taught it only
phrases.notes: He means the חכמים's ruling in the משנה that slaughtering for עבודה זרה makes him liable.

phrases.english: where he slaughtered the first for idol worship
and the second for his table,
but if the first was for his table
and the second for idol worship – he is exempt,
since he receives the greater punishment.
phrases.notes: The second act deserves death for עבודה זרה, so he does not also get lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the עבודה זרה case from step 4 and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability applies only when the עבודה זרה slaughter was first. If it was second, he gets only the death penalty and is exempt from lashes.

steps.title: That point is too obvious to teach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects that even schoolchildren know you get only the greater punishment, so רבי שמעון בן לקיש's limit adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: even schoolchildren know this!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges רבי שמעון בן לקיש. He says the rule about the greater punishment is so basic that it does not need to be taught. This sets up his own new teaching in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack does not say the rule is wrong. It says the rule is obvious, so it cannot be the real new point here.

keyTerms.meaning: Schoolchildren, an image for something everyone already knows

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן
phrases.english: This, even schoolchildren
know it!

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן יוֹדְעִין אוֹתָהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן לקיש's limit in step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that a person gets only the greater punishment is basic knowledge, so stating it teaches nothing new.

steps.title: Sometimes he is liable even when the idol slaughter came second
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that even if the עבודה זרה slaughter came second, he can get lashes. This happens when he was warned only about אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, sometimes, even if he slaughtered the first for his table and the second for עבודה זרה, he is liable. For example, when they warned him about אותו ואת בנו and did not warn him about עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives what he sees as the real new point. In some cases the order does not exempt him from lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Punishment by a court needs a warning (התראה) beforehand. If he was warned only about אותו ואת בנו, he cannot get death for עבודה זרה. Since the bigger punishment is not actually given, the lashes for אותו ואת בנו stay.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned him beforehand, as needed for a court punishment
A warning before a sin. Without it, the court does not punish
Liable, here meaning he gets lashes

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'greater punishment' rule may depend on which punishment can actually be given, not just which sins were done.

phrases.english: Rather, there are times when even
he slaughtered the first for his table
and the second for idol worship – he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּאַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ מִשּׁוּם ״אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״,
phrases.english: For example, where they warned him about 'it and its offspring,'
phrases.notes: 'They' means the witnesses, who warn him right before the second slaughter.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ מִשּׁוּם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: and did not warn him about idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, פְּעָמִים שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ שָׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן לְשֻׁלְחָנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the obvious teaching from step 6 with a new case where he is liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he was warned only about אותו ואת בנו, he gets lashes even though the second slaughter was for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Exempt either way
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש disagrees. Since he would be exempt from lashes if warned about עבודה זרה, he is also exempt when not warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: since he would be exempt if they warned him, he is also exempt if they did not warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן לקיש rejects רבי יוחנן's case. That is why his own teaching in step 6 was not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, the act itself carries the bigger sin of עבודה זרה. That alone cancels the lashes, whether or not the warning was given. So the missing warning does not bring the lashes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, used to reason from one case to another

steps.whatToRemember: Second slaughter for עבודה זרה with no warning about עבודה זרה: רבי יוחנן says he gets lashes for אותו ואת בנו. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says he is exempt either way, because the act itself carries the greater sin.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
since when they warn him – he is exempt,
phrases.notes: He means warned about עבודה זרה. Then he would get death, not lashes.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ נָמֵי – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: when they do not warn him, he is also exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּכִי אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוחנן's liable case from step 8 and so defends step 6 as a real teaching.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוחנן's case where he was warned only about אותו ואת בנו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption comes from the act itself carrying the greater sin, not from the warning. So a missing warning changes nothing.

steps.title: The same argument appears in another case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש follow their own known reasoning. It brings רב דימי's report of their argument about a sin that carries death or lashes along with a money payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: They each follow their own reasoning. When רב דימי came, he reported a case of people who could get death or lashes but were not warned, and the act also involved a money payment. רבי יוחנן says he is liable to pay. ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects our argument to a second, parallel argument between the same two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case, the man was warned only about אותו ואת בנו, not about עבודה זרה. In רב דימי's case, the man was not warned about death or lashes, but his act also carries a money payment. The question is the same in both: does the bigger punishment that he cannot actually get still cancel the smaller one?

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning (from another place)
Those whose sin carries the death penalty
Those whose sin carries lashes
Literally 'unintentional'; here, not legally warned, so the court cannot punish
Another matter; here, a money payment from the same act

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
as when Rav Dimi came, he said:
those liable to death who acted unwittingly,
phrases.notes: Here 'unwittingly' means nobody warned him, so the court can't give the death penalty or lashes.

phrases.english: and those liable to lashes who acted unwittingly,
and there is another matter involved,
phrases.notes: The 'other matter' is a money payment that comes from the very same act.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he is liable,
and Reish Lakish says: he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָזְדוּ לְטַעְמַיְיהוּ, דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the argument in steps 8-9 matches an argument the same two sages have elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the bigger punishment did not get a warning, רבי יוחנן makes him pay the money and ריש לקיש exempts him.

steps.title: The reason behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he pays because he was never warned about the bigger sin. ריש לקיש says that since a warning would have exempted him, he is exempt without one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, because they did not warn him. ריש לקיש says he is exempt: if they had warned him he would be exempt, so when they did not warn him he is also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each sage rules the way he does in רב דימי's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, without a warning the bigger punishment does not really exist, so nothing cancels the payment. For ריש לקיש, the bigger sin itself cancels the smaller liability, whether or not there was a warning. This is the same reasoning ריש לקיש used in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (introducing a reason)
Also

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ריש לקיש lets him off because he is 'innocent'. He is exempt because the bigger sin swallows up the smaller one, even though the bigger punishment can't actually be given.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he is liable,
since they did not warn him;
and Reish Lakish says: he is exempt,
since, if they had warned him, he would be exempt,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ נָמֵי פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: when they did not warn him, he is also exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר: חַיָּיב, דְּהָא לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the two rulings quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: no warning means the bigger punishment does not cancel the payment. ריש לקיש: the bigger sin cancels it either way.

steps.title: Why we need both arguments: part one
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the אותו ואת בנו case, we might think ריש לקיש exempts him only there, but agrees with רבי יוחנן in the money case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to teach both. If we were taught only this case, we would say ריש לקיש says exempt only here. In the other case, we would say he agrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why both arguments had to be recorded. It shows what we would have wrongly thought if we only had our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case, death and lashes are both punishments to the body, so it makes sense for one to cancel the other. A money payment is a different kind of thing. So we might have thought ריש לקיש would not let death or lashes cancel a payment.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (to teach both cases)
If it had taught us (only)
I would say (a mistaken first guess)

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if it had taught us only in this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is ours: אותו ואת בנו, with the second slaughter for עבודה זרה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: only in this case does Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish say he is exempt,
but in that case,
phrases.notes: 'That case' is רב דימי's case with the money payment.

phrases.english: I would say he agrees with Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that the two arguments match, explains why both still had to be taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From our case alone, we might limit ריש לקיש's ruling to body punishments only.

steps.title: Why we need both arguments: part two
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the money case, we might think רבי יוחנן says liable only there, but agrees with ריש לקיש about lashes. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was stated only in the money case, we would say רבי יוחנן says liable only there. In our case, we would say he agrees with ריש לקיש. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation and concludes that both arguments had to be stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the money case alone, we might think רבי יוחנן makes him pay only because money is a different kind of punishment. When it is lashes against death, both body punishments, we might think even רבי יוחנן says the bigger one cancels the smaller. Since each case could have been read the opposite way, we need both.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees
In this (case); the word switches between the two cases

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says that without a warning for the bigger sin, he still gets the smaller punishment or payment. ריש לקיש says the bigger sin cancels the smaller one even without a warning. Each side holds this in both cases, and both cases had to be taught.

steps.title: Is the red heifer's slaughter really 'unfit'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון can call the slaughter of the פרת חטאת a שחיטה שאינה ראויה. In a ברייתא, רבי שמעון says the slaughtered פרה can receive טומאת אוכלין, because it once had a שעת הכושר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is the slaughter of the red heifer really a slaughter that does not make the animal fit? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says a red heifer can become impure the way food becomes impure, since it once had a time when it was fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה about the פרת חטאת. It challenges that ruling with another teaching from רבי שמעון himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון exempts the slaughter of the פרה from אותו ואת בנו because it is a שחיטה שאינה ראויה, meaning it does not make the animal fit to eat. But in the ברייתא, רבי שמעון treats the slaughtered פרה as food, because it can receive טומאת אוכלין. If he treats it as food, why does he call its slaughter 'unfit'?

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose ashes are used to purify people from impurity caused by a dead body.
A slaughter that does not make the animal fit to eat.
The kind of impurity that only food can receive.
A time when something was fit or valid.
Since; because.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether the פרה is a real פרת חטאת. The question is whether רבי שמעון contradicts himself: in one place he calls its slaughter 'unfit,' and in another he treats it as food.

phrases.english: And the red heifer of purification
is it a slaughter that is unfit?
phrases.notes: This is the reason behind רבי שמעון's exemption in the משנה, even though the משנה itself doesn't spell it out.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Shimon says:
a red heifer can become impure with the impurity of food
since it had a time in which it was fit

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש discussion, the גמרא turns to a new part of the משנה: רבי שמעון's exemption for the פרת חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reason in the משנה that slaughtering the פרת חטאת is a שחיטה שאינה ראויה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a ברייתא, רבי שמעון says the slaughtered פרה receives טומאת אוכלין because it had a שעת הכושר. That means he treats it as food, which seems to contradict calling its slaughter 'unfit.'
